props.snippet: Millcreek's buildings with modelled lidar roof forms and measurements in feet, on the city's lidar terrain. Unvalidated planning estimates; not surveyed or field-verified.
props.description:
Planning estimates. Everything here comes from the 2023 Salt Lake Valley QL1 lidar (flown October-November 2023) and the City of Millcreek's processing of it. These are unvalidated planning estimates, not surveyed or field-verified data. Do not use them for engineering, legal or property decisions.

Millcreek's buildings with modelled lidar roof forms and measurements in feet, on the city's lidar terrain. Select a building for its model source, heights and available roof measurements. Use the slides for a tour, or drag to look around.

Explore the buildings

Use Search to find an address, choose a slide for a neighborhood, then zoom in and select a building. Drag to rotate the scene; Home returns to the starting view. The legend explains the gray height classes. Daylight changes the illustrative lighting.

What the models show

The three-way hybrid contains 21,561 buildings: 20,730 detailed roofer LoD2.2 models, 647 Esri LOD2.0 roofs and 184 Esri LOD1.2 blocks. Each building uses the selected model for that footprint. Simpler roofs retain city coverage where a detailed roof did not pass the model checks. The pop-up reports the model source and any fallback reason.

Read a building pop-up

Median and upper roof heights describe the lidar points above the local ground. Modelled ridge and eave heights describe the reconstructed roof; they are different measurements. Footprint area is horizontal ground coverage. Roof surface area includes the sloping roof faces, so it can exceed the footprint area. The support percentage reports how much of the footprint contains roof points, not a probability that the model is correct.

Detailed roof measurements are present only for the 20,730 retained roofer models. A blank value on an Esri fallback means unavailable; zero means the model has none of that measured area. Flat roof area uses slopes below 5 degrees; compass-facing areas use slopes from 5 to 70 degrees. Bearings are degrees clockwise from north. Facing areas are screening measurements, not estimates of usable solar area or electricity production. Roof angles remain in degrees.

Downloads and limitations

Building measurements in feet and square feet (CSV) · 3D building package (SLPK) · Full model methods and field definitions

Join the CSV to the models using FP_ID. The SLPK keeps its original metric coordinates and source fields; the CSV provides converted measurements. A detailed-looking roof is still an inferred planning model. Dormers, overhangs, small structures and occluded roof sections can be simplified or incorrect. Lighting and shadows illustrate geometry and are not a validated solar or shadow study.

Dates and units

The source is the 2023 Salt Lake Valley QL1 lidar, flown in October and November 2023. These maps describe that survey, not present-day conditions. Buildings removed, trees planted or construction completed since then may differ. Basemap imagery can be from a different date.

Height legends and building heights use feet; building areas use square feet. Canopy-zone summaries use acres and percentages. One international foot is exactly 0.3048 meter. The original coordinate system, elevation reference and metric analysis files remain intact so all layers stay aligned. Rounded display values do not imply survey precision.

Questions or corrections: City of Millcreek GIS. Include the map location and building ID when available.

props.title: Millcreek 3D buildings with roof forms (2023 lidar), planning estimate
props.snippet: 21,561 Millcreek, Utah, buildings in 3D. Roof forms (gables, hips, dormers, flat roofs) from the 2023 lidar where supported, with simpler Esri roofs or blocks elsewhere. Unvalidated planning estimate; not surveyed or field-verified.
props.description:
Planning estimate. This layer is an unvalidated estimate derived from lidar by City of Millcreek GIS. It has not been surveyed, engineered or checked in the field. Use it for planning, screening and display, not for legal, engineering, property-boundary, permitting or code-compliance decisions.

What it shows

Every Salt Lake County building footprint in Millcreek, Utah, that has a lidar roof, as a 3D building: 21,561 of them. For most (20,730) the roof has a modelled shape: gables, hips, dormers, stepped and flat roofs, taken from the 2023 lidar. For the rest the roof is simpler (Esri's LOD2.0 roof forms for 647, flat LOD1.2 blocks at the median roof height for 184), because the lidar could not support a roof form or the roof form failed a check. The LEVEL field says which model a building has.

Fields

Each building carries its footprint's County attributes and lidar roof-height statistics (see the data dictionary), so a pop-up can show its height. Buildings whose LEVEL is roofer LoD2.2 also carry roof attributes; for the others they are empty.

Field Stored type Meaning
OBJECTID OID Package row identifier; use FP_ID to identify the source footprint.
Name String Model object name.
FP_ID Integer Footprint identifier used by the massing and roof comparison runs.
PARTS Integer Number of converted model parts.
RF_ROOF_TYPE String Roof type inferred by roofer.
RF_ROOF_PLANES Integer Roof plane count reported by roofer.
RF_RIDGELINES Integer Ridgeline count reported by roofer.
RF_RMSE_LOD22 Double Roofer model fit RMSE (metres); not independent accuracy.
RF_H_GROUND Double Roofer ground elevation (metres).
RF_H_ROOF_MAX Double Maximum roof elevation reported by roofer (metres).
RF_PT_DENSITY Double Point density reported by roofer (points per square metre).
RF_EXTRUSION String Roofer extrusion status.
SOURCE_ID String County source footprint identifier, as text.
PARCEL_ID String County parcel identifier carried with the footprint.
CITY String County city attribute.
FOOTPRINT_M2 Double County footprint area (square metres).
ROOF_COV_PCT Double Share of footprint cells with classified lidar roof support (percent).
ROOF_Z50_M Double Median classified lidar roof elevation (metres).
GROUND_Z50_M Double Median ground elevation under the footprint (metres).
HEIGHT_P50_M Double Median lidar roof height above ground (metres); not code-defined height.
HEIGHT_P95_M Double 95th percentile lidar roof height above ground (metres).
HEIGHT_STATUS String Processing and support flags, including UNVALIDATED.
LEVEL String Model used: roofer LoD2.2, Esri LOD2.0 or Esri LOD1.2.
CHECK_VERDICT String Check result recorded when the hybrid was assembled.
ROOFER_VERDICT String Roofer comparison verdict against the source lidar.
ESRI_VERDICT String Esri LOD2.0 comparison verdict against the source lidar.
FALLBACK_REASON String Reason the model falls back from roofer to Esri.
ROOF_PLANES Integer Roof planes of 1 m2 or more in plan, from the lidar roof (roofer). Null for Esri fallback buildings.
ROOF_PLAN_M2 Double Area of those planes seen from above. Null for Esri fallback buildings.
ROOF_AREA_M2 Double True (sloped) area of those planes. Null for Esri fallback buildings.
ROOF_SLOPE_MEAN Double Slope from horizontal, weighted by plane area. Null for Esri fallback buildings.
ROOF_SLOPE_MAIN Double Slope of the largest plane. Null for Esri fallback buildings.
ROOF_AZIMUTH_MAIN Double Compass bearing of the largest plane's downslope direction (0 north, clockwise); empty if flat. Null for Esri fallback buildings.
RIDGE_HT_M Double Highest roof point minus the building's ground elevation. Null for Esri fallback buildings.
EAVE_HT_M Double Lowest roof point minus the building's ground elevation. Null for Esri fallback buildings.
BLDG_HT_M Double Same as the ridge height: highest roof point above the building's ground. Null for Esri fallback buildings.
FLAT_AREA_M2 Double Surface area of planes under 5 degrees. Null for Esri fallback buildings.
SOUTH_AREA_M2 Double Surface area of planes of 5 to 70 degrees facing 135 to 225 degrees. Null for Esri fallback buildings.
EAST_AREA_M2 Double Same, facing 45 to 135 degrees. Null for Esri fallback buildings.
WEST_AREA_M2 Double Same, facing 225 to 315 degrees. Null for Esri fallback buildings.
NORTH_AREA_M2 Double Same, facing 315 to 45 degrees. Null for Esri fallback buildings.
RF_VOLUME_M3 Double Volume of roofer's LoD 2.2 solid. Null for Esri fallback buildings.
TINY_FACES Integer Roof faces under 0.5 m2 in plan (quality screening). Null for Esri fallback buildings.
SLIVER_FACES Integer Roof faces narrower than about 0.4 m (quality screening). Null for Esri fallback buildings.
STEEP_FACES Integer Roof faces steeper than 75 degrees (quality screening). Null for Esri fallback buildings.

Using it in a scene

Put the Millcreek bare-earth terrain elevation layer in the scene's Ground, above World Elevation. The buildings were built on that terrain. Ground estimates and vertical datum labels can still produce offsets; inspect placement before relying on it.

How it was made

  1. Roof points. A lidar point is roof when at least two of three classification methods call it building.
  2. Roof forms. For each footprint, roofer finds the roof planes in those points, splits the footprint into roof parts and extrudes them to a closed 3D model, with each footprint's ground from nearby ground points.
  3. Check and choice. Each roofer model is compared with the lidar roof on the same 0.5 m cells. A building takes roofer's model when it passes (not above the lidar roof by more than 1 m, not short of it over more than 5% of its cells, not at ground level over 10% of its footprint, and not clearly worse than a flat block); otherwise it takes Esri's LOD2.0 roof if that passes, otherwise a flat block.
  4. Packaged as a scene layer package in WGS84 and published on October 25, 2026.

Accuracy and checks

  • On the cells where the lidar saw roof, the buildings are within 0.5 m of the lidar roof on 96.7% of cells and within 1 m on 98.1% (flat blocks alone: 56.9% and 80.4%). The lidar is also what the roofs were built from, so this measures fidelity to the lidar, not an independent accuracy.
  • An assistant reviewed 109 imagery crops, including 97 buildings using roofer. These are preliminary visual observations, not City-reviewed accuracy results. The separate blank rating file remains for the City reviewer.
  • The package and hosted layer have 21,561 buildings. Their FP_ID count and sum match the source; source IDs are unique. ArcGIS Pro package validation passed without warnings. Hosted model counts and roof-area totals match the validated package.
  • Roof attributes apply to 20,730 retained roofer buildings: 4,855,408.3 m² of roof surface, including 1,230,559.8 m² under 5 degrees. The 831 Esri fallback buildings have null roof attributes and are excluded from these totals.

Limits

  • Planning estimates, not surveyed buildings. Heights are roof-minus-ground from lidar, not code-defined building heights.
  • Complex roofs can come out fragmented: many small facets where one or two planes are real. Chimneys and dormers are modelled when the lidar sees them and may be missing or merged where it does not.
  • Footprints are the County's. Footprints that hold several buildings, or buildings built or removed since, are as the County drew them; stale footprints can cause the fallback to model a roof over ground or a demolished structure. These need review; they are not corrected building records.
  • Under trees, glass roofs and dark roofs the lidar sees less, and those buildings are the ones that fall back to simpler models.
  • Roof attributes (slope, azimuth, areas) are geometry from the lidar roof. They are not a solar production estimate: no shading, panel layout or weather.

Coordinates

Horizontal: WGS84, taken from NAD83(2011) with the transformation WGS_1984_(ITRF08)_To_NAD_1983_2011, as every other layer in the set. Vertical: heights are NAVD88 (Geoid18) metres; the package's vertical label is EGM96 (see the scene-layers README).

Download

The scene layer package (SLPK, 20.2 MiB) contains the same three-way hybrid used by this hosted layer. Release: October 25, 2026; 21,228,379 bytes.

props.title: Millcreek buildings and canopy cover zones (2023 lidar), planning estimate
props.snippet: Building footprints with lidar roof heights, and tree canopy cover by ownership zone, for Millcreek, Utah, from 2023 lidar. Unvalidated planning estimate; not surveyed or field-verified.
props.description:
Planning estimate. This layer is an unvalidated estimate derived from lidar by City of Millcreek GIS. It has not been surveyed, engineered or checked in the field. Use it for planning, screening and display, not for legal, engineering, property-boundary, permitting or code-compliance decisions.

What it shows

Two layers for Millcreek, Utah:

  • Buildings (22,042 polygons): Salt Lake County's building footprints inside or crossing the city limits, each with roof-height statistics measured from the 2023 lidar. 21,562 footprints have a height; 480 have no lidar roof inside them and their height fields are empty (possible reasons include buildings demolished since the County drew them, very small structures and roofs hidden under trees).
  • Canopy cover zones (13 polygons): the share of the ground covered by tree canopy at least 2 m tall, for the whole city and for groups of land by ownership (private, public and its owner groups, uncertain owner, and land outside every parcel). Citywide canopy cover is 25.59% of the observed area (2,103 acres).

Typical uses: a citywide look at building heights and massing, finding tall or unusual buildings for review, canopy goals and comparisons between ownership groups. Heights are roof minus ground, not building heights as a building code defines them.

How it was made

  • Roofs. Every lidar point was classified three independent ways: this project's own first classification, the IGN FRACTAL model, and Esri's pretrained building model. A point counts as roof when at least two of the three call it building. The roof surface is the highest first or single return in each 0.5 m cell from those points.
  • Ground. The bare-earth terrain is interpolated at 0.5 m from the ground-classified returns (under a building it is interpolated from the ground around it).
  • Heights. For every 0.5 m cell whose centre lies inside a footprint (and inside the city), roof elevation minus terrain elevation. A footprint's median (HEIGHT_P50_M), 95th percentile and maximum are taken over the cells that have both a roof and terrain value. Footprint shapes and County attributes are unchanged.
  • Canopy. A canopy height model at 0.5 m: vegetation returns minus terrain, with roofs masked out. Canopy is any observed cell at least 2 m above the ground. Cover for a zone is canopy cells as a share of the zone's observed cells, counted by cell centres.
  • Zones. From the City's parcel layer: parcels grouped by owner with fixed rules (named public agencies, schools, housing authorities and districts are public; everyone else, including utilities, churches and nonprofits, is private; missing or mixed owners are uncertain), dissolved by group and clipped to the city. "No parcel" is the city outside every parcel, mostly streets and other rights-of-way. Zones overlap: the whole-city zone contains all the others and the public owner groups sit inside "Public / government parcels", so do not add areas across rows.

Accuracy and checks

  • Roof classification, against 1,217 hand-labelled roof and non-roof parts on one 1 km tile (a deliberately hard sample, not a citywide accuracy): 92.8% of roofs found; 2.8% of non-roof parts called roof.
  • Vegetation classification, same tile: 95.9% of tree parts called vegetation; 10.7% of non-vegetation parts called vegetation; shrubs 76.5%.
  • Roof support. 2,380 footprints have a lidar roof on less than 80% of their area (LOW_ROOF_SUPPORT). Their heights are less reliable: lower roofs, porches and carports are often the part missed. Of the footprints with at least 95% support, the 3D blocks built from these heights are within 1 m of the median roof for all but 13 of 14,229.
  • Canopy coverage. About 99.4% of every zone is observed by the lidar; the low and high bounds in the layer show how far the unobserved cells could move each figure (about half a point at most).
  • Copies. Every value and every footprint shape was checked against the source library before upload (0 rows differ), and the projection to Web Mercator was checked vertex by vertex (all within 0.07 mm of Esri's own projection with the ITRF08 transformation).
  • None of these figures is a field validation. No building height has been compared with a survey or a plan set.

Limits

  • Heights are roof-minus-terrain estimates, not code-defined building heights (which are measured to a defined point of the roof from a defined grade). Chimneys, rooftop equipment, parapets and branches over a roof raise the maximum; the median is the safest single figure.
  • Footprints are the County's. A footprint can hold several buildings, a building can have several footprints, and buildings built or demolished since the County drew them show up as missing or empty roofs. 22,042 is a count of footprint records, not of buildings.
  • Many County fields are empty in this snapshot (BLDGHEIGHT, SOURCE, most ADDRESS and BuiltYear values). They are carried unchanged so the layer joins back to the County's.
  • Canopy at 2 m includes tall shrubs and excludes lower plants. Leaf-off trees in early November may be under-counted where few returns came back from bare branches.

Slope classes and contours at 6.56 ft intervals on Millcreek's lidar terrain, from the valley floor to the east bench. Use the slides for the hillside neighbourhoods, or drag to look around.

Explore terrain

Use the slides to visit the east bench, canyon mouth and foothills. Rotate the scene to see relief, and use the layer list to compare slope colors, contours and hillshade. The elevation profile tool reports a drawn transect in feet; choose the ground profile when comparing bare-earth terrain.

Read the legend

Slope is percent rise: 20% means 20 ft of vertical rise over 100 ft of horizontal distance, not a 20-degree angle. The six color classes run from under 10% to 30% and over. They summarize the ground surface and do not establish a regulatory slope finding.

Thin contours are 6.56 ft apart vertically and heavy index contours are 32.81 ft apart. These are the original 2 m and 10 m intervals converted to feet, not newly generated 5 ft or 10 ft contours. The vector tiles have no elevation pop-ups or line labels.

Resolution and limits

The bare-earth terrain has an approximately 1.64 ft grid (0.5 m), with slope computed over a roughly 9.84 ft neighborhood. Small slope patches below about 43 sq ft were removed in the display polygons. Grid spacing is not an accuracy claim. Hillshade and scene lighting help reveal landforms; they do not show a measured surface color.

Bare-earth processing removes buildings and vegetation where classification permits. Walls, bridges, steep banks, water and gaps in ground returns can still create artifacts. Outside the city terrain coverage, the scene can use Esri World Elevation, which has a different source and resolution. These layers support reconnaissance, not grading design, drainage engineering or surveyed elevations.
